neighbours.label: a relative pronoun 'who' (or relativizer) opening a clause right after a noun for people (people who, everyone who, those who)
fire: Grants are offered to students who cannot afford the full fees.
She thanked the nurses who had cared for her father.
Anyone who finishes early may leave the room quietly.
The fans who waited in the rain finally got their autographs.
There are many farmers who still plough with horses.
He was one of the few soldiers who returned home that winter.
Teachers who use the new method report better results.
We need volunteers who can drive on weekends.
quiet: Grants are offered to poor students for the full fees.
She thanked the nurses for caring for her father.
Early finishers may leave the room quietly.
The fans waited in the rain and finally got their autographs.
Many farmers still plough with horses.
He was one of the few soldiers to return home that winter.
With the new method, teachers report better results.
Who can drive us to the station on Saturday?

notes: Card flags broad (1.1% of tokens at 0.1 of max). Peaks on ' who' after people/individuals/everyone, also ' of' and ' that'. Near misses keep the people noun but drop the relative clause or use interrogative who.
